parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
On 12 January 2010, a powerful earthquake caused devastation in Haiti.
Many people were killed or injured on the day of the earthquake. This is called the
primary effect.
Other people suffered in the days and months after the earthquake. This is called the
secondary effect.
Some of the consequences of the earthquake included:
• About 200 000 people were killed on the day of the earthquake.
• About 300 000 people were injured on the day of the earthquake.
• After the earthquake, 1.5 million people were left homeless and 4000 schools were
damaged or destroyed.
• After the earthquake, 216 000 people were infected with cholera and over 5000 died
from cholera.
• After the earthquake, people were unable to get food, which led to starvation.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Damage and loss of life were caused by the combined primary and secondary effects of
this earthquake.
Discuss whether the primary effects or the secondary effects of the earthquake had a
larger impact.
Support your answer with reasons.
